'''FreedomCon''' was a charity gaming convention run by [[DeckTech]] on 15&ndash;18 November 2001 at the Sheraton Oceanfront Hotel in Virginia Beach, Virginia.<ref name="fc-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon home page], decktech.net (after the event). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011201221615/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 1 December 2001]</ref> It was held after [[Decipher]] cancelled DecipherCon 2001, which had been scheduled for the same dates and hotel.<ref name="tf-dcon">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/DecipherCon_2001_72163.asp DecipherCon 2001], TheForce.Net (15 June 2001)</ref><ref name="holland">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Special message from Decipher CEO Warren Holland], TheForce.Net (3 October 2001)</ref> DeckTech billed its Star Wars, Star Trek, Young Jedi and Jedi Knights tournaments as World Championship events for those games.<ref name="fc-about">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/about.php About FreedomCon], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020219012905/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/about.php Internet Archive, 19 February 2002]</ref> The Star Wars CCG event is counted as the [[2001 Decipher World Championship]].

== Star Wars CCG World Championship ==

[[Bastian Winkelhaus]] was declared World Champion of Star Wars CCG. The top four were:<ref name="fc-home" />

# [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] (World Champion)
# [[Martin Akesson]]
# Hayes Hunter
# [[Brian Hunter]]

A 2020 forum thread recalls the third and fourth places the other way round, Brian Hunter third and Hayes Hunter fourth.<ref name="fc-forum-34">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300380#p1300380 allstarz97's post], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211006195438/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 Internet Archive, 6 October 2021]</ref>

[[Scott Lingrell]] was also in the final eight, and later posted his Light Side Rebel Strike Team list on DeckTech as [[Scott Lingrell FreedomCon 2001 - Final 8 Deck]].<ref name="fc-forum">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History], forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020; players' recollection of the 2001 top 8). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211006195438/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 Internet Archive, 6 October 2021]</ref>

== Recognition ==

Decipher said on 9 November 2001 that it would not recognize FreedomCon as the World Championships, because the official 2001 World Championships were cancelled with DecipherCon; it added that the event could be sanctioned through its tournament program.<ref name="fc-stmt">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Deciphers_Statement_About_Freedom_Con_70203.asp Decipher's Statement About Freedom Con], TheForce.Net (9 November 2001; statement by Monica Jones, Decipher V.P. Marketing). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012022154/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Deciphers_Statement_About_Freedom_Con_70203.asp Internet Archive]</ref> DeckTech's own site carried the same notice, that FreedomCon was "not recognized or authorized by Decipher Inc."<ref name="fc-about" /> The [[Players Committee]]'s list of World Champions nonetheless includes Winkelhaus's FreedomCon win as the 2001 title.<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org (World Champions list: "2001 - Bastian Winkelhaus def. Martin Akesson, held at FreedomCon - Virginia Beach, VA"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222454/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Internet Archive, 17 August 2023]</ref> The February 2002 announcement of the 2002 World Championship qualification system gave him a Day Two bye as the previous year's FreedomCon champion.<ref name="hs">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp The Hyperspace Lane to the World Championships], TheForce.Net (9 February 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009001957/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

== The event ==

Entry cost $30 pre-registered or $35 at the door. All proceeds went to the American Red Cross Disaster Relief Fund: with 160 people attending, the World Championship events raised $1,343.<ref name="fc-home" /> DeckTech also ran championship events for the other Decipher games; the winners were Brian Muller (Jedi Knights), Katie Billings (Young Jedi) and Ian Vincent (Star Trek).<ref name="fc-home" />

DeckTech later listed a second event, FreedomCon Philadelphia, for 4&ndash;6 October 2002 at NeoQuest Games in Lansdale, Pennsylvania.<ref name="fc-attend">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/attend.php Players Attending], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030113235106/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/attend.php Internet Archive, 13 January 2003]</ref>
